title: FEATHER: A Reconfigurable Accelerator with Data Reordering Support for Low-Cost On-Chip Dataflow Switching
problem: Different layers of ML models require different optimal dataflows (tiling, ordering, parallelism, shapes), with suboptimal choices causing up to 100x performance degradation. Reconfiguring hardware to switch between dataflows incurs significant overhead from on-chip data layout reordering and datapath reconfigurations, preventing accelerators from exploiting optimal dataflows.
motivation: ML accelerators can achieve dramatic speedups by using optimal dataflows per layer, but reconfiguration overhead has prevented practical multi-dataflow systems.
method: FEATHER introduces NEST, a spatial array architecture, and BIRRD, a multi-stage reduction network that performs flexible data reduction with implicit layout reordering to enable seamless dataflow switching with negligible latency overhead. The paper extends Timeloop with layout assessment to create Layoutloop for systematic dataflow-layout co-design evaluation. The design is modeled in Layoutloop and validated end-to-end on ZCU104 FPGA.
key_novelty: BIRRD multi-stage reduction network that performs flexible data reduction with implicit layout reordering, enabling low-cost on-chip dataflow switching.
contributions: NEST spatial array for flexible multi-dataflow execution
BIRRD reduction network for layout-aware data reduction with minimal reconfiguration overhead
Layoutloop framework extending Timeloop with layout assessment capabilities
End-to-end FPGA deployment achieving 2.65-3.91x throughput improvement with only 6% area overhead
primary_theme: Reconfigurable dataflow acceleration with low-overhead layout switching
